title: Raise Sans with your strongest suit
author_notes: Reviewed during EC-033 implementation; see docs/COACHING_REVIEW.md. Independent hand; ratings are authored judgments, not probabilities or guaranteed outcomes.

feedback.title: Count beats suit rank
feedback.summary: Five Clubs legally beats four Sans and makes your six-card, top-heavy Club suit trump.
points: Control: Ace-King-Queen-Jack of Clubs head six trumps.
Probable: the Heart Ace and promoted Clubs can support the target; the Diamond King is conditional.
Rule: five tricks beats four regardless of trump rank; no equal-count raise can beat Sans.

feedback.title: Six asks for some extra work
feedback.summary: Six Clubs is plausible with top trump control, but the Diamond King and lower Clubs still need favorable play.
points: Control: Ace-King-Queen-Jack of Clubs head six trumps.
Probable: the Heart Ace and promoted Clubs can support the target; the Diamond King is conditional.
Rule: five tricks beats four regardless of trump rank; no equal-count raise can beat Sans.

feedback.title: A high-ranked suit is not a strong holding
feedback.summary: Five Spades is legal, but 7-2 gives little trump control. The ranking does not improve the cards.
points: Control: 7-2 of Spades has no high trump.
Risk: your strong Clubs become side cards that opponents may ruff.
Rule: a legal higher bid can still be a weak strategic choice.

feedback.title: A larger target magnifies the weakness
feedback.summary: Six Spades asks for more tricks while choosing your short, low suit as trump.
